mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past quarter indicates an easing monetary policy stance, which reduces borrowing costs and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals weakening labor market strength, prompting investor concerns about economic growth and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such episodes are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the unemployment rate does not exceed 4.5% in the subsequent period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and a drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals dual easing, amplifying confidence in economic growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect fails to produce statistically significant positive returns (Rank IC < 0.05) over the 20-day horizon in more than 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers higher discount rates on equities, compressing future cash flows and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal does not materialize in the tightening cycle (e.g., FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% or returns are positive) or the regime is incorrectly identified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in quarterly GDP growth above 3% indicates robust demand for goods and services, lifting corporate earnings expectations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or GDP growth does not sustain above 3% in the subsequent period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the industrial production index below 100 signals weakening supply-side growth, reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The industrial production index recovers above 100 within the 20-day window or returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in housing starts below 1000 units indicates cooling demand for real estate, raising concerns about consumer spending and triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing starts rebound above 1000 within the 5-day window or returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in GDP demand (GDPC1 above 23528) and industrial production (INDPRO above 103.88) signals robust economic expansion, boosting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of high demand and supply does not produce statistically significant positive returns (Rank IC < 0.05) over the 60-day horizon in more than 50% of cases.
